absent: LRU batch movement targets and generational sequence management beyond the observed checks.
Address-space tree API contracts and workingset update callback behavior.
Try-invalidate iterator, sleeping behavior, and truncation caller contracts.
Per-filesystem fadvise, release, and free operations and advice code meanings.
Writeback engine internals, tag maintenance, and flush-range helper behavior.
NUMA policy lifecycle, mode encodings, home-node rules, and allocator reclaim details.
Cgroup, LRU-vector, zone, and NUMA event accounting semantics.
Folio flag layout, reference counting, and large and hugetlb state transitions.

findings.text: Exposes deactivation for file-backed folios. Folios that are unevictable or outside LRU management are left untouched. When generational reclaim is active a reference-clearing check may complete the work, otherwise the folio is handed to batched deactivation handling.

Two build variants exist for generational reference clearing. The active variant treats negative generation as already clear, clears reference and workingset state, and reports whether the folio generation still matches the current minimum sequence for its file type. The inactive variant always reports no progress.
Provides in-place compaction of a folio batch that discards encoded exceptional entries while preserving relative order of genuine folios and updating the stored count to the number retained.

Shadow-entry reclamation over an index interval does nothing for shmem and DAX mappings. For other mappings every encoded value entry within bounds is replaced by empty and hosts that remain shrinkable are queued for inode reclaim.
Shadow reclamation serializes with page-cache mutation by holding the host inode lock for the whole scan and nesting the address-space tree lock in IRQ-safe mode while entries are modified.

Offers conditional eviction of a folio from a mapping. The request is refused for absent mappings, dirty or under-writeback state, excess references beyond cache membership plus private state plus caller, and unreleasable private state; otherwise removal from the mapping is attempted with its outcome returned.

Release of folio private state requires a locked folio. Folios that need no release succeed at once while folios under writeback fail. When work remains the owning mapping operation is preferred when present with buffer release as the fallback, and need is defined by private state or a mapping that always requires release.
Exposes invalidation of cached pages over a page-index interval by delegating to a shared try-invalidate helper with no per-folio callback.

User entries for file access-pattern hints accept descriptor, offset, length and advice. Empty descriptor lookup yields bad-descriptor status. Both narrow and wide length variants share one kernel helper that prefers per-file advice handling and otherwise uses generic handling.
The file-cache translation unit enables creation of its trace points.

Batched removal detaches listed folios from their mapping. The mapping link is cleared while the index is retained for truncation lookup, tree entries are removed, and the mapping page count is reduced by the total size of removed folios. Encoded entries and unrelated pages met during the scan are skipped.

Batched page-cache deletion holds the host inode lock and the address-space tree IRQ lock while unaccounting and detaching entries, queues shrinkable hosts for inode reclaim before releasing, and frees folios only after locks are dropped.

Two observers distinguish consuming versus preserving mapping write-error state. The consuming observer clears space-shortage and I/O flags while reporting them with I/O taking precedence when both are present. The preserving observer only reports with the same precedence.

Write initiation exposes full-mapping and ranged forms plus a budgeted form. One ranged form requests fully synchronous writeback, the full-mapping write form covers the entire range, the flush form delegates to ranged flushing over the entire range, and the budgeted form requests non-waiting initiation over the entire range with a caller-supplied counter.
Presence testing over a byte range rejects inverted ranges and ignores encoded shadow entries. The check runs without pinning and only establishes that a genuine folio was recently present.

Tagged folio collection walks forward from a caller cursor, skipping encoded entries that can appear racily, accumulating genuine entries into a batch until full or the end is reached, and advancing the cursor past the scanned region with explicit handling that avoids index overflow at the maximum value.

Writeback waiting scans folios tagged under writeback in batches, waits on each member, releases the batch and yields scheduling between iterations. Variants share this wait loop and differ only in post-wait error reporting for mappings or files and in preserving versus consuming error state.

Per-file write-error tracking uses a lockless sequence comparison for the common unchanged case and a file-locked slow path to advance the cursor with tracing. Legacy mapping flags are always cleared afterward for compatibility. A separate setter records a new mapping error with tracing.

Need for writeback is equated with a nonzero mapping page count. A ranged check rejects inverted ranges, skips encoded entries, and reports true when any folio in range is dirty, locked, or under writeback.

Combined write-and-wait over a range does nothing for inverted ranges and skips initiation when the mapping holds no pages. Otherwise it initiates ranged writeback and, except when I/O failure is indicated, waits for completion before folding mapping or per-file error state into the result.

Atomic cache-slot replacement exchanges an old folio for a new one at the same index. Mapping membership is transferred with an extra reference held on the newcomer, file and shared-memory accounting is adjusted for applicable folio types, and the old folio is released through its optional free handler.

Replacement requires both folios locked and the newcomer initially without mapping. The address-space tree lock is held in IRQ-safe mode across the pointer exchange and accounting updates, with the optional free handler invoked only after unlocking.

File-cache folio allocation prefers an explicit NUMA policy when supplied, otherwise spreads across allowed nodes with rebinding-aware retry when that mode is enabled, and falls back to default allocation. Policy-backed pages are marked reference-counted and large folios are promoted to a remappable state.

Policy-driven allocation resolves an effective node and optional restriction mask from the policy mode. Preferred modes override the input node, bind restricts the mask subject to zone and cpuset validity with a warning against node-pinned allocation, and huge orders may first attempt local-only allocation with compaction but without reclaim before the general path.

Interleaving selection guards against concurrent cpuset rebinding by validating the allowed-set sequence around node choice. Weighted selection reads a shared table under read-side protection with unit fallback, supporting both stateless index-derived targets based on total weight and stateful progression using per-task memory of current node and remaining weight.

Observed file-cache objects expose an address space carrying page tree i_pages with host link and resident count nrpages plus flag word flags and error sequence wb_err and operations a_ops, and a file carrying mapping f_mapping with error cursor f_wb_err and state lock f_lock and operations f_op.

Several paths assume strict folio state. Release and deletion expect locked folios, replacement expects both participants locked, and reference-count initialization expects a non-tail page with zero count. Violation triggers diagnostic or fatal checks rather than silent repair.
Advice dispatch reports EBADF for an empty descriptor. Mapping error observers report ENOSPC for space shortage and EIO for I/O failure.

Mapping write-error state moves from set to observed to cleared or advanced. Wait helpers preserve the set state until completion, initiation failures still lead to waiting except for I/O failure, and per-file cursors advance independently while legacy flags are cleared.

Range presence checks, tagged collection and interleaving weight reads run inside read-side critical sections without holding tree locks, tolerating concurrent reclaim or table replacement through retry, skip or fallback logic.
